title: DGFT Reviews Wheat Export Quota: Check Your Allocations
excerpt: Wheat exporters, DGFT has reviewed export quotas. Verify your allocations now.
body:
## What changed
The DGFT has issued Trade Notice 18/2026-27, announcing a review and re-allocation of the export quota for wheat under HS Codes 10011900 and 10019910. This means the previously allocated quotas may have been adjusted, affecting your export plans.

## Why it matters for shipments
For those exporting wheat, this change could impact your current and future shipments. It's crucial to verify if your allocated quota has been altered. Any changes might require adjustments in your export schedules or documentation.

## What to do next

title: EXIM Bank Takes Over Interest Subvention for Export Credits
excerpt: EXIM Bank replaces RBI for export credit interest subvention. Check your eligibility now.
body:
## What changed
The DGFT has announced that the implementation agency for the Interest Subvention Support for Pre- and Post-Shipment Export Credit under the Export Promotion Mission (EPM) has transitioned from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to the Export-Import Bank of India (EXIM Bank). This change is detailed in Trade Notice 17/2026-27 dated August 7, 2026.

## Why it matters for shipments
This shift could affect how you apply for interest subvention on your export credits. If you're dealing with pre- or post-shipment export finance, especially in sectors like chemicals, textiles, or seafood, this change might alter the documentation or process requirements. The exact impact on your shipments will depend on how EXIM Bank implements these changes.

## What to do next
1. Open the official notice [here](https://content.dgft.gov.in/Website/dgftprod/0ba8138f-3784-4cdb-81b1-8ec1a1ff738d/TN%2017-2026-27%20%20Interest%20subvention.pdf).
2. Check whether your CTH / docs / policy line is touched.
3. Ask Neo’s CHA before changing Bill of Entry / Shipping Bill practice.
impact: Exporters using interest subvention should review the new EXIM Bank process. Confirm eligibility and documentation changes.

title: New Initiative for Export Branding and Packaging
excerpt: The DGFT has launched a new initiative aimed at enhancing export branding and packaging for Indian products.
body:
The Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) has announced Trade Notice 12/2026-27, introducing a Global Outreach program focused on branding, labeling, and export packaging. This initiative is part of the Export Promotion Mission (EPM) known as Niryat Disha.

The goal is to help Indian exporters improve their product presentation in international markets. Effective branding and packaging can significantly impact sales and customer perception. 

Exporters in various sectors, including textiles, chemicals, and agro products, can benefit from this program. The initiative aims to provide guidance and resources to enhance the visibility and appeal of Indian products abroad.

For more details, you can access the full notice [here](https://content.dgft.gov.in/Website/dgftprod/381252d1-91dc-4a23-9084-f4efc23eb864/Trade%20Notice-%20Global%20Outreach%20for%20Branding,%20Labelling%20and%20Export%20Packaging-%2014.07.2026.pdf).
impact: This initiative can help exporters improve their market presence and increase sales through better branding and packaging.

title: Clarifications on Interest Subvention Support for Export Credit
excerpt: The DGFT has released Trade Notice 13/2026-27, providing important clarifications on interest subvention support for export credit under the Export Promotion Mission.
body:
The Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) has issued Trade Notice 13/2026-27, dated July 14, 2026. This notice offers clarifications regarding the interest subvention support available for pre- and post-shipment export credit under the Export Promotion Mission (EPM) known as Niryat Protsahan.

This support is crucial for exporters as it helps reduce the cost of borrowing, making it easier to finance their operations. The notice outlines the eligibility criteria and the application process for exporters seeking this support. It aims to enhance the competitiveness of Indian exports by easing financial burdens.

For detailed information, exporters are encouraged to review the full notice available on the DGFT website. Understanding these provisions can significantly benefit businesses involved in various sectors, including textiles, chemicals, and agro products, among others. 

Stay informed about such updates to leverage available support effectively.
impact: This notice can help exporters reduce financial costs, enhancing their competitiveness in international markets.

title: New DGFT Notification: Prohibition on Import of Goods Produced Using Forced Labour
excerpt: The DGFT has issued a new notification prohibiting the import of goods produced using forced labour. This affects various industries and aligns with ethical trade practices.
body:
On July 13, 2026, the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) released Notification 23/2026-27. This notification introduces important changes to the Foreign Trade Policy (FTP) 2023, specifically the insertion of Para 2.20B and Para 11.64. 

The key focus of this notification is the prohibition on importing goods produced using forced labour. This move aims to promote ethical trade practices and ensure that imported goods meet certain human rights standards. 

Importers and exporters across various sectors, including textiles, seafood, and chemicals, should take note of this development. It is crucial to ensure that your supply chains are compliant with these new regulations to avoid potential penalties or disruptions in trade. 

For more details, you can access the full notification [here](https://content.dgft.gov.in/Website/dgftprod/15ac9a16-6edb-432a-8f98-3bf2d0bf8bda/Notification%2023%20eng.pdf). Stay informed and ensure your business practices align with these new guidelines.
impact: This notification impacts importers by enforcing stricter compliance regarding the sourcing of goods, promoting ethical practices in trade.

title: New Amendments Under India-Oman CEPA
excerpt: The DGFT has announced amendments to the Handbook of Procedure 2023 regarding TRQs under the India-Oman CEPA.
body:
The Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) has issued Public Notice 20/2026-27, which introduces amendments to Para 2.92 and Appendix-2A of the Handbook of Procedure 2023. These changes pertain to the inclusion of Tariff Rate Quotas (TRQs) under the India-Oman Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA).

This notice aims to facilitate trade between India and Oman by providing clearer guidelines on the TRQs. Importers and exporters in various sectors, including cashew, steel, chemicals, automobiles, mining, textiles, agro products, seafood, cement, and sanitary wares, should take note of these amendments as they may impact their trade operations.

For detailed information, you can access the full notice [here](https://content.dgft.gov.in/Website/dgftprod/a449d22b-2eca-4cc6-9ee8-c91b252f4e60/PN-Oman.pdf). Staying updated with these changes is crucial for compliance and to leverage potential benefits under the CEPA.
impact: This notice may affect importers and exporters by providing new opportunities and guidelines for trade under the India-Oman CEPA.

title: New DGFT Trade Notice: Electronic Filing for Preferential Certificate of Origin
excerpt: Starting July 15, 2026, the DGFT will implement electronic filing for the Preferential Certificate of Origin under the India-UK CETA.
body:
The Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) has announced a significant update regarding the issuance of the Preferential Certificate of Origin (CoO) under the India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA). Effective from July 15, 2026, importers and exporters will be required to file for the CoO electronically.

This change aims to streamline the process and enhance efficiency in trade between India and the UK. The electronic filing system is expected to reduce paperwork and processing times, making it easier for businesses to comply with trade regulations.

For those involved in sectors such as textiles, chemicals, and agro products, this transition could simplify the export process and improve access to the UK market. It is crucial for businesses to stay informed and prepare for this new electronic system to ensure a smooth transition.

For more details, you can refer to the official notice [here](https://content.dgft.gov.in/Website/dgftprod/b6f82c21-f67b-4bcf-b94f-ddd08d98c4ef/trade%20notice%20(1).pdf).
impact: This notice will impact exporters and importers by simplifying the process for obtaining a Certificate of Origin, particularly in sectors trading with the UK.

title: Extension of TRQ Authorisation for Gold Imports Under India-UAE CEPA

body:
The Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) has issued Public Notice 18/2026-27, which extends the validity of Tariff Rate Quota (TRQ) Authorisation for the import of gold under the India-UAE Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA). This extension applies to imports classified under Tariff Head 7108 and is valid until September 30, 2026.

Importers should take note of this extension to ensure compliance and to maximize their import opportunities under the CEPA framework.

title: DGFT Notification 22/2026-27: Amendments in Import Policy for Chapters 74 and 76
excerpt: Recent amendments in the import policy under Chapters 74 and 76 of the ITC(HS) 2022 could impact your import strategies. Learn what changed and how it might affect your business.
body:
## What Changed?
The Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) has issued Notification 22/2026-27, dated June 30, 2026, announcing amendments in the import policy under Chapter 74 (Policy Condition 3, sub-para (c)) and Chapter 76 (Policy Condition 1, sub-para (c)) of the ITC(HS), 2022. While the full text of the notification is not available here, it is crucial for importers to review these changes as they may affect import regulations for certain goods.

## Who Should Care?
These amendments are particularly relevant for industries dealing with copper and aluminum products, as Chapters 74 and 76 typically cover these materials. Importers in the **Steel**, **Chemicals**, **Automobiles**, **Industrial raw materials**, and **General trade** sectors should pay close attention to these changes, as they might influence import procedures or compliance requirements.

## Next Steps
To fully understand the implications of these amendments, it is advisable to read the official notification [here](https://content.dgft.gov.in/Website/dgftprod/449397ee-ca25-4243-a1ab-d87b49e6d347/english_0005.pdf).
